items.name: Bloom Energy Corp
items.news: Bloom Energy is set to join the S&P 500 effective Monday, September 21, which typically forces passive index funds to buy shares on the effective date. The fuel-cell maker has been a major beneficiary of the AI data-center power buildout and is already up roughly 190% year-to-date.
items.risk: Index-inclusion pops can fade quickly once passive buying is absorbed, especially after such a large YTD run-up.
items.entry: Dip to $256.68–262.94, or break above $288.00 on volume

items.name: Roivant Sciences Ltd
items.news: Shares rallied 24% after subsidiary Pulmovant reported Phase 2 data showing a clinically meaningful, statistically significant reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance for mosliciguat in patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease. This is a genuine binary clinical catalyst with a large single-day move that could see continuation or profit-taking Monday.
items.risk: Biotech data-driven pops are prone to sharp reversals on profit-taking or scrutiny of trial details/small sample sizes.
items.entry: Dip to $38.91–39.51, or break above $41.60 on volume

items.name: Intel Corp
items.news: Intel jumped in Friday's session amid broad semiconductor strength, and Tigress Financial reiterated a Buy rating while raising its price target from $118 to $145. Chip stocks broadly outperformed as the SOXX ETF also rallied.
items.risk: Semiconductor momentum can reverse fast on any AI-capex or guidance disappointment from peers.
items.entry: Dip to $105.80–107.76, or break above $111.37 on volume

items.name: Marvell Technology Inc
items.news: BofA reiterated a Buy on Marvell with a $365 price target, arguing the custom AI silicon opportunity could reach $300 billion by 2030. The stock has already nearly tripled in 2026 on AI infrastructure demand.
items.risk: Stock has run very hard already, making it vulnerable to any AI capex growth-rate disappointment or broader tech pullback.
items.entry: Dip to $238.08–242.40, or break above $247.89 on volume

items.name: Exxon Mobil Corp
items.news: Brent and WTI remain above $100 a barrel for a second straight week as Saudi-Houthi fighting near the Bab al-Mandeb strait and renewed Iranian rhetoric around the Strait of Hormuz keep a geopolitical risk premium in crude. items.risk: Any de-escalation headline or diplomatic breakthrough could sharply reverse the oil-driven bid.
